summary: This document extends the DOTS signal channel so clients can control their filtering rules while attack mitigation is active. A client can activate or deactivate existing rules during a DDoS attack, with the rules defined earlier over the DOTS data channel when idle.

eli5.summary: During an attack, a victim can switch prepared blocking rules on or off. This document lets it do that over the emergency call line.

questions: activate ddos filtering rules during attack
what is the dots signal channel
how to deactivate dots filtering rules during an attack
subtitle: Lets a DDoS victim switch prepared filtering rules on or off through the DOTS signal channel mid-attack.

tldr.problem: Filtering rules set up over the DOTS data channel cannot be changed during a DDoS attack, because that channel is not built for attack conditions, so a harmful rule such as an accept-list can stay in force.
tldr.mechanism: A client sends an acl-list in a signal channel mitigation request, naming an existing ACL and an activation-type that overrides the one set earlier over the data channel.
tldr.outcome: A client can activate or deactivate its own pre-created filters while mitigation is active, using the signal channel designed to keep working under attack.

today: RFC 9133 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2021 as an extension of the signal channel in RFC 9132. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Filters Need Control During an Attack
sections.content:
In the DOTS architecture, clients and servers use two protocols. The data channel (RFC 8783) handles bulk exchange, including filter management for dropping, rate-limiting or permitting traffic. The signal channel (RFC 9132) is built to stay resilient and keep contact even as attack traffic saturates the link, using heartbeat requests.

The data channel is not expected to cope with attack conditions. Filters installed through it may not work as expected during an attack or may make it worse, and the client cannot use it to change them then.

A typical case is an accept-list installed in idle time. During a volumetric attack the mitigator may find that the accept-listed sources are attacking, for example because an attacker spoofed them or compromised them. The server reports a conflict (conflict-cause set to 2, conflict-with-acceptlist), but the client may be unable to withdraw the rule over a saturated link.
sections.eli5: You hired a guard and gave a list of friends allowed in. If some of those friends turn out to be troublemakers, you need a way to cross them off while the crowd is outside, and the normal phone line is jammed.

sections.title: Binding the Two Channels
sections.content:
This extension only controls rules, it does not create them. Filtering rules are made earlier by the same client over the data channel. The client MUST use the same cuid on both channels, which ties them together. The two channels may or may not reach the same server, so servers in a domain are assumed to coordinate, though how is out of scope.

A rule is identified by its ACL name. Activating or deactivating an ACL over the signal channel overrides the activation-type that was set over the data channel. Afterwards the client may use the data channel to set the type back or delete rules, depending on the deployment.
sections.eli5: The client writes the rules ahead of time on one form, then later just points at a rule by name and says on or off over the emergency line.

sections.title: The acl-list Attribute
sections.content:
The extension adds an acl-list to the CBOR body of a mitigation request. Each entry has two sub-attributes:

  • acl-name: the name of an ACL defined over the data channel. Mandatory when acl-list is present.
  • activation-type: optional. One of deactivate, immediate or activate-when-mitigating, as defined in RFC 8783. Both immediate and activate-when-mitigating take effect right away while a mitigation request is being processed.

These are comprehension-required parameters, so a server that does not understand them replies 4.00 (Bad Request).
sections.eli5: Each instruction has two parts: which rule (by name) and what to do with it (off, on now, or on when a defense starts).

sections.title: How Requests Are Processed
sections.content:
Clients MUST NOT use filter control in idle time, and servers MUST discard such requests with 4.00 (Bad Request). During an attack, a client may include the ACL attributes in a mitigation request, always with a new mid. It is NOT RECOMMENDED to put them in an initial request or in one that adjusts the scope, so that ACL failures do not delay mitigation. Clients are RECOMMENDED to subscribe to asynchronous notifications of the mitigation.

If the server cannot find the acl-name for that client, it MUST reply 4.04 (Not Found). Otherwise it MUST apply the update immediately. The new type stays as the ACL's activation type even after the mitigation ends, and the server MUST refresh the ACL lifetime as for a data channel refresh. If it cannot apply the update, it MUST reply 5.03 (Service Unavailable) and put the failed ACL update in the diagnostic payload.

On a 5.03 to an initial or scope-adjusting request, the client MUST immediately resend the request without the ACL attributes. After the Max-Age in the 5.03 expires, it retries with a new mid including them. If the activation type is changed at the server during mitigation, the server tells the client in a notification or a poll response.
sections.eli5: The emergency line only works during an attack. If the rule is missing or the change fails, the server says so, and the client first makes sure the main defense starts, then tries the rule change again later.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
Section 4 gives three examples, all using JSON to illustrate the data. They are not deployment recommendations.

  • Conflict handling: a client installs an accept-list an-accept-list for UDP traffic to port 443 from 2001:db8:1234::/48. After a conflict notification, it sends a PUT with activation-type deactivate and a new mid, and the server confirms with 2.04 (Changed).
  • On-demand accept-list: a filter installed as deactivate is switched on with immediate during a UDP attack so that specific traffic is still forwarded.
  • Lacking capacity: if the server or mitigator cannot cope and the client still receives attack traffic, the client activates a prepared rate-limit filter, and later deactivates it, for instance after the status changes from attack-exceeded-capability to attack-mitigation-in-progress.
sections.eli5: The examples show the same trick three ways: cross a bad friend off the list, turn on a special pass for good visitors, or turn on a speed limit when the crowd is too big.

sections.title: Encoding and IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC defines the YANG module ietf-dots-signal-control, which augments the signal channel module from RFC 9132. It is used only to provide a data model and encoding, not for managing servers over NETCONF or RESTCONF. In the module, activation-type defaults to activate-when-mitigating.

IANA registered CBOR keys in the DOTS Signal Channel CBOR Key Values subregistry: activation-type as key 52 (major type 0) and ietf-dots-signal-control:acl-list as key 53 (major type 4). The existing acl-name uses key 23. IANA also registered the XML namespace URN and the YANG module name.
sections.eli5: Each field gets an official number so both sides write it the same way on the wire.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The extension cannot create new filters, so clients should prepare in advance by creating filters that can be activated when an attack is detected. A client can only access resources it created, so it cannot change rules made by other clients in its domain, and servers must tie filters to the client that created them. Failing to do so would have a severe impact on client domains.

A compromised client could use filter control to make an ongoing attack worse, or ignore an ACL conflict notification. These are variations of threats already discussed in RFC 9132 and RFC 8783, and operators should monitor and audit DOTS agents.
sections.eli5: You can only flip switches you installed yourself, and if a client is hacked it could flip them the wrong way, so someone should keep an eye on it.

items.label: acl-name
items.desc: Text string (major type 3); name of an ACL from the data channel.

items.label: activation-type
items.desc: Unsigned (major type 0); enumeration overriding the ACL's activation type.

items.label: ietf-dots-signal-control:acl-list
items.desc: Array (major type 4); list of ACL entries to control.
